nc_razors_edge_canyon.blurb: In Linville Gorge, Razors Edge Canyon is a mostly-gear cliff within the Gold Coast, the stretch under the Rock Jock Trail. Walls on the canyon's south side run roughly 200 to 300 feet, giving long, multi-pitch days. A handful of corner and crack lines share the cliff with several harder face climbs, and bolts are few. Around eighteen climbs are recorded, nearly all trad plus a couple of aid lines, ranging from easy fifth class up to 5.11, with most falling between 5.9 and 5.11. The rim is also a well-regarded overlook for gazing across the gorge. Expect a committed, remote feel rather than a roadside crag.
nc_razors_edge_canyon.approach: Reach the Rock Jock Trail by the steep drainage-ditch path from the road, then turn left and follow the Razors Edge access trail a few minutes to the top of the cliff. A third-class path leads down into the canyon.

nc_stone_depot.blurb: Stone Depot is a quiet multi-pitch crag tucked behind Cedar Rock in Pisgah National Forest, reached from Butter Gap. Its seventeen climbs are mostly trad with a handful of bolted lines, and the grades are friendly: the bulk sit around 5.7 and 5.8, with a few at 5.9 and 5.10 and a single 5.11. Many routes take two or more pitches, and belay and rappel stations are generally easy to spot from the base. The wall faces northwest, so it feels warm on cool spring days and can bake in summer. Because Cedar Rock pulls the crowds, climbers here often have the cliff to themselves, with a view across to Looking Glass.

nc_family_wall.blurb: At Rumbling Bald near Chimney Rock, Family Wall is a slab-angled stretch uphill of the main east trail, sandwiched between two other sectors. About sixteen routes are recorded, mostly trad with a couple of sport lines and some top-rope options. The grades are gentle: most routes are around 5.7, with a few easier or harder ones and a small number reaching 5.10 and 5.11. That makes it a sensible place for newer leaders and for groups with mixed ability. Because the moderates are popular, the wall can get crowded, and the slab climbing rewards good footwork over strength.

nc_granite_city.blurb: Granite City is a small, informal bouldering spot at the foot of Blackrock Mountain, close to Whiteside Mountain and the Cashiers and Highlands area. Large boulders, some 10 to 40 feet tall, form narrow corridors where the problems are packed together. Most are V0 to V2 and not especially tall, which suits beginners and families, with a few harder lines up to around V6 and one roped route near 5.10. A steeper, enclosed section behind the main passage has taller walls that can be rigged with trees. Expect moss and dirt, since it is lightly developed and best treated as a quick, exploratory day.
nc_granite_city.parking_note: Drive Whiteside Cove Road past where it turns to gravel; a small pull-off on the right holds only two or three cars.
nc_granite_city.approach: A short, steep trail follows the drainage ditch up from the pull-off to the tops of the boulders; a second path to the right reaches the other side. Either takes about five minutes.

nc_flakeview_area.blurb: Flakeview is a popular sector of Rumbling Bald, just outside Chimney Rock, known for good moderate routes alongside a few harder bolted lines. It offers both face climbing and solid slab climbing, mostly on trad lines with four sport routes among its seventeen climbs. Grades run from easy fifth class to a lone 5.11, and the largest group sits around 5.10, with several 5.7s and a scattering between. Some routes are two pitches. Rumbling Bald as a whole is favored as a winter destination, and the trail up passes the neighboring Screamweaver cliffline before turning left to reach this wall.
